LESSON: LANGUAGE USE 5.4.1 PLURALS OF IRREGULAR NOUNS

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade two
Subject: General
Strand: Strand 5
Topic 5.4: Language Use 5.4.1 Plurals of irregular nouns
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Language Use 5.4.1 Plurals of irregular nouns, part of Strand 5 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade two General.

Key inquiry question: What things do we buy? 2. How do we refer to things when they are many?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Language Use 5.4.1 Plurals of irregular nouns together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication: The learner’s speaking skills are enhanced as they speak clearly and effectively about their shopping experiences using

plurals of irregular nouns.

• Digital literacy: The learner’s interaction with digital devices is enhanced as they type sentences onto a digital device

Values:
Respect: The learner’s acceptance skills are enhanced as they understand and appreciates others during group activities.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Financial literacy: The learner’s financial literacy skills are enhanced as the learner role plays shopping activities.

Link to other Learning Areas:

Plurals of irregular nouns are learnt in Kiswahili and Indigenous Language Activities.

Suggested Learning Resources:

Assistive technology such as universal cuffs/wrist braces/arm braces, weighted pencil/pen grips, page-turners, adapted digital devices with filter

keys/key guards/larger mouse/head control input devices such as head wand

Other Related Service Providers: Resource person, speech therapist, Learner support assistance, Occupational Therapist, Physiotherapist.
